## kb_to_source

- Every normative sentence of the 13 docs above traced to a source clause or variant figure; hypothetical examples and boundary tables are provable derivations.
- Addition/rewrite found: **vision_early_cancellation_benefit_offset_3eeae95a, Rule sentence — "and the Vision Plans benefits paid on it outran the premium"**. "on it" (the unit, which the computation doc defines as "the subscriber's Vision Plans enrollment") narrows the benefits population; the source states no such scope ("the vision benefits paid are the plan payments on vision services remarked as …"; tier: "the vision benefits paid on services within the unit's coverage window exceed …") and the compute (ben_unit) sums every vision claim of the customer in the window. On this task's records the narrowed reading changes the scored credit (154.32 vs 74.56) and the grace-cure payment (187.86 vs 267.62).
- Cross-problem operational guidance ("if unmet, first call …"): none.
- Opening world state written as policy fact: none (all examples hypothetical; no task date/amount reproduced).
- Rationale clauses in depended-on docs ("the automatic draft stays suspended and the invoice issued last is collected with the grace-cure payment"; "months beyond the paid-through date are corrected when the coming year is paid") are verbatim source ladder text, not additions.

## bijection_verdict

**KB-BIJECTION RED** — KB-B0-1: docs/billing/vision_early_cancellation_benefit_offset_3eeae95a.json, opening Rule sentence, "paid on it" restricts the vision-benefits population to the unit (subscriber enrollment), a scope the source rule does not carry and the source compute contradicts (customer-wide claims). Everything else in scope is lossless. First revision for this difficulty; no earlier revision.

Policy-side note (does not change this verdict) — SRC-1 (genuine ambiguity, low severity): billing_ext_vision_term_credit rule never states whose vision services enter "the vision benefits paid" (the unit's own subscriber enrollment, the other enrollments on the same family-tier plan, or every vision enrollment of the customer); the compute takes every vision claim of the customer (XSUM is customer-scoped, no account or plan filter). With the unit defined as one enrollment record, the rule invites the narrow reading the KB adopted.

### bijection_verdict
**KB-BIJECTION PASS** — KB-B0-1 closed (the offset doc now carries the source's population, no narrower and no broader). No new defect; no regression.

Source side, SRC-1 closed: the rule names the population (the unit's enrollments) and the account test, and compute v_other and ben_unit match the stated test.
- Note (no id, latent, no task effect): the compute's ben_unit still sums every in-window vision claim of the customer. A claim on a non-unit, non-cancelled vision enrollment funded by this same account, inside the unit's window, would be counted by the compute but not by "services of the unit". The rule's clause "the services are read from all of the subscriber's vision claims" covers only the other-account case. Neither task world has such an enrollment (task 0's other enrollment 555f3204 is cancelled, a different plan, and dated 2024).
